headline: Sanderson’s return much needed for Senators’ injury-riddled blueline
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Jake Sanderson's return is much needed for an injury-riddled Senators blueline, but even with him back, Ottawa is now playing without captain Thomas Chabot.

The loss is a real one. Chabot has played 25:20 a night on defense so far this season, and the Senators have been better with him on the ice: their share of the 5-on-5 scoring chances (expected goals, a measure of chance quality) rises by about 7 percentage points when he plays. He has 4 points in 9 games, and his one goal sits almost exactly at what his chances suggest (1.03 expected), so his production looks sustainable rather than lucky. Ottawa is 6-3-0, though the team numbers are modest: a 50.6% share of expected goals overall and 49% at 5-on-5, with goalies bailing them out by 2.2 goals above expected. That margin is thin without their top pair defenseman.

Going by how the coach has used his players, Tyler Kleven (21:05 a night) is next in line for Chabot's minutes. Chabot also works the second power-play unit and kills penalties, so expect those shifts to be reshuffled too.
